notes.meaning: Peter and John walked up to the temple at three in the afternoon, the regular Jewish hour of prayer. Even after Jesus rose from the dead, the apostles continued to pray together at the temple and look for opportunities to share the good news.

A man who had been unable to walk since birth was carried every day to the temple gate called Beautiful. Friends placed him there so he could beg for money from the people entering the courtyard to worship.
When the man saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked them for some money. He had no thought of being healed and only expected a small handout to help him get through another day.
Peter and John looked straight at the beggar, and Peter told him to look at them. The man gave them his full attention, expecting that they were about to give him some money.
Peter told the man that he had no silver or gold to offer. Instead, by the authority and power of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, Peter commanded the lame man to get up and walk.
Peter took the man by the right hand and helped him stand. Right away, strength rushed into his feet and ankles, curing his lifelong condition without any need for practice or physical therapy.

The man jumped up onto his feet, stood firm, and began to walk for the first time in his life. He went into the temple courts with the apostles, leaping with joy and loudly praising God for healing him.

All the people in the temple saw the man walking around and praising God. They quickly recognized him as the beggar who had sat for years at the Beautiful Gate, and they were completely filled with wonder and shock.
The healed man held on tightly to Peter and John out of deep love and gratitude. A crowd of amazed people rushed together toward them in the covered walkway known as Solomon's Colonnade.
When Peter saw the crowd gather, he asked why they were so surprised by the miracle. He warned them not to stare at the apostles as if human power or personal godliness had made the man walk.

Peter explained that the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had brought honor to His servant Jesus. The crowd had handed Jesus over to the authorities and rejected Him before the Roman governor Pilate, even after Pilate wanted to let Him go free.
The people rejected Jesus, who was completely pure and innocent before God and the law. Instead of choosing the Holy One, they asked the governor to release Barabbas, a convicted murderer.

Peter pointed out the terrible irony that the crowd killed the Author of life Himself. But death could not hold Him, because God raised Jesus from the dead, and the apostles saw Him alive with their own eyes.
Peter declared that the power and authority of Jesus had made this well-known lame man completely strong. Faith that comes through Jesus gave the man total healing in plain view of the whole crowd.

differ.view: Some Pentecostals emphasize that the lame man himself exercised personal faith in Jesus in order to receive healing.

notes.meaning: Peter kindly called the crowd his brothers and recognized that they and their rulers had acted in spiritual ignorance. Their lack of understanding did not remove their guilt, but it meant they were still eligible for God's forgiveness.
Even though the people intended evil, God used their actions to fulfill His ancient plan. All the prophets had declared long before that God's Messiah, His chosen King, would have to suffer.

Peter told the people to repent—which means to turn away from sin and turn back to God—so their sins could be completely wiped away. True repentance allows believers to receive peace and spiritual refreshment from the presence of the Lord.

differ.view: Some evangelicals teach that the times of refreshing refer specifically to the earthly kingdom that would have begun if Israel had repented as a nation, while others see it as the spiritual peace and renewal believers enjoy throughout the church age.

notes.meaning: Peter taught that Jesus must stay in heaven until the final time comes when God restores all creation, just as the holy prophets promised. When that time arrives, God will send Jesus Christ back in glory to complete His kingdom.

differ.view: Some evangelicals teach that Peter was offering the earthly millennial kingdom to Israel, which would have arrived immediately if the Jewish nation had repented.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular modern teachers use the phrase 'restoration of all things' to claim that every person and fallen spirit will eventually be reconciled to God and saved.

notes.meaning: Moses had warned their ancestors long ago that God would raise up a supreme Prophet like him from among the people of Israel. Moses commanded everyone to listen to this Prophet, warning that anyone who refused to obey would be cut off from God's covenant family.
Samuel and all the prophets who followed him also spoke about these very days. The events surrounding Jesus and His kingdom were the direct fulfillment of Israel's prophetic scriptures.

Peter reminded his listeners that they were heirs of the prophets and of the covenant promise God made with Abraham. In that covenant, God promised that all families across the earth would be blessed through Abraham's descendant.

God raised up Jesus and sent Him first to the Jewish people to offer them His greatest blessing. That blessing was not political freedom, but the gift of grace that turns each person away from wickedness and sin.
